This organization focused on planting trees, environmental conservation, and women's rights. She was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004. She also served as the assistant minister for environment and natural resources in the Kenyan government.

Kisumu is known as the third-largest city in Kenya and is a significant industrial and commercial center. It is the cultural center of the Luo people of East Africa and serves as a key link in the trade route between Lake Victoria and Mombasa due to its water and rail connections. It is also recognized as a "Millennium City."

Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o, whose birth name was James Ngugi, is a Kenyan author and academic. He is considered East Africa's leading novelist and a significant figure in modern African literature. He began writing primarily in English but later shifted his focus to writing in Gikuyu and became a strong advocate for literature in native African languages. His works include novels like The River Between, plays, short stories, memoirs, and essays. The Uganda Railway was a metre-gauge railway system and a former British state-owned railway company. It connected the interior of Uganda and Kenya with the Indian Ocean port of Mombasa in Kenya. After several mergers and splits, the line is now managed by the Kenya Railways Corporation and the Uganda Railways Corporation.

The Battle of Adwa was the decisive battle of the First Italo-Ethiopian War, fought on March 1, 1896, near the town of Adwa. It took place between the Ethiopian Empire, led by Emperor Menelik II, and an Italian colonial force commanded by General Oreste Baratieri. The conflict arose from a dispute over the interpretation of the Treaty of Wuchale, which Italy used to try and establish a protectorate over Ethiopia. M-Pesa is a mobile phone-based money transfer, payment, and micro-financing service. It was launched in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom, the largest mobile network operator in Kenya, and has since expanded to several other countries. It allows users to deposit, withdraw, transfer money, and pay for goods and services using a mobile device. It functions as a branchless banking service, using a network of agents for cash transactions.

Dedan Kimathi Waciũri was a leader of the Kenya Land and Freedom Army during the Mau Mau Uprising against British colonial rule in Kenya in the 1950s. He was born on October 31, 1920, and was captured by the British in 1956, being executed in 1957. Kenyan nationalists view him as a freedom fighter, while the British colonial authorities labeled him a terrorist. He is credited with helping to create formal military structures within the Mau Mau and was one of the Field Marshals.
